sections.label: 01 Auto-matched
paragraphs: PO, vendor, and amount align within policy. The operator confirms quickly. Primary action is approve swiftly and have AI summary available.

sections.label: 02 Needs Review
paragraphs: A person has to judge. That covers variance, first-time vendors, policy edge cases, and other exceptions. The UI shows the specific issue and suggested next steps, and may ask for a reason or checklist before approval.

sections.label: 03 Blocked
paragraphs: Hard stop. Duplicate suspicion, no PO match, or other conditions that should not proceed on a single click. Resolution options stay explicit and the AI assistant explains why approval is unavailable.

sections.label: Layout options
paragraphs: I tested three layout directions. Chat-forward with the AI assistant dominant. Dashboard-first with KPI strip and invoice table. Minimal decision card with compact facts. The control room layout with queue plus split view won because it matched how people actually worked.

sections.label: Interaction pattern
paragraphs: Selecting an invoice opens the AI assistant pane with context loaded. Quick actions in chat trigger typed replies, a brief thinking state, and AI confirmation. The action footer updates so approval shows as completed in place.

sections.label: Deliverables
paragraphs: The final deliverable was a clickable HTML prototype of the workspace. Three desktop states: Auto-matched, Needs review, and Blocked. Each shows how the shared shell carries different content density and actions.

sections.label: What I would test
paragraphs: Do AI replies feel faster than form buttons, or do they add uncertainty? When an invoice is Blocked, can operators find the right resolution without support?

sections.label: Next possible iteration
paragraphs: Next tasks are batch actions on Auto-matched, vendor management, tolerance rules per client, and analytics on overrides.
